title: Large language models for combinatorial optimization of design structure matrix

live_model.evidence: "we repeated the experiments in Table 2 using three different backbones: two open-source LLMs (Mixtral-7x8B and Llama3-70B) and one closed-source LLM (GPT-4-Turbo (OpenAI 2024)), accessed via its API." Table 3 (Ablation on the Backbone LLM) gives per-case GPT-4-Turbo results.

prompt.location: Sec. 2/3.2 (method describes prompt inputs: node names, edge list, network description, iterative in-context refinement; "only the topological information...is engineered into the input prompt" for the no-knowledge ablation)
prompt.note: Prompt construction is described structurally; no single verbatim prompt string is quoted in the retrieved text.

claim.metric: DSM sequencing solution-quality score (lower is better), GPT-4-Turbo backbone, single-trial with domain knowledge, UAV DSM case
claim.location: Table 3 (Ablation on the Backbone LLM), row 'GPT-4-Turbo / with', 1-trial, Unmanned Aerial Vehicle column (9.6 +/- 3.2); n=10 independent random-seed runs per Sec. 3.2

data.source: Four DSM case studies (UAV, Microfilm Cartridge, Heat Exchanger, Automobile Brake System) reconstructed from published engineering references (Browning 1998; Ulrich & Eppinger 2016; Amen et al. 1999; Black et al. 1990); no code/data repository link found in the text

notes: GPT-4-Turbo is one of four backbone LLMs in an ablation (Table 3), run directly via API by the authors across 4 cases x 2 knowledge conditions x {1,5,20}-trial settings x 10 seeds. Two soft gaps keep this at 'maybe': the exact prompt text is described but not quoted verbatim, and the four DSM inputs must be reassembled from cited published sources rather than a bundled release.
